rulers.name: Lalliya

rulers.name: Toramana
rulers.note: Infobox "c. 903: Toramana"; end year is the next accession (c. 921).

rulers.name: Bhimadeva

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Hindu Shahi row; its Turk Shahis row ends 874). "In 870 CE, Ya'qub ibn al-Layth ... marched onto Kabul"; the Saffarids held it "until 878 CE". The Shahis keep Gandhara around Udabhandapura. The page gives no area.

union.text: Nandana, Jailam (Jhelum) and Takeshar, the Salt Range and Jhelum country that Bharat of Lahore wished to wrest from Jayapala

correction.text: from Lamghan in the west, to Kashmir in the east

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Kabul recaptured by Lalliya in 878 and described as Shahi again by 900 (Hindu Shahis page); the Jayapala page puts the realm "from Lamghan in the west, to Kashmir in the east" (Lamghan = Laghman). Laghman and the Kashmir frontier are the researcher's reading; the Hindu Shahis page says only "Kabulistan, Gandhara and Punjab". No area on either page. Review fix 2026-10-19: the Salt Range and Jhelum country (a 70 km disc round Nandana, the capital of 1002-1014) is added, so the capital lies inside the state. The Hindu Shahis page says the dynasty ruled "Kabulistan, Gandhara and Punjab", and the Jayapala page has Bharat of Lahore wishing "to wrest control of Nandana, Jailam and Takeshar" from Jayapala around 990-991, so these places were Shahi before the Lahore annexation. The rest of the Punjab east of the Indus is not drawn before 999: Lahore was annexed only in 998-999 (and reinstated as a feudatory c. 990-991), Multan was Daud's (emirate-of-multan to 1010), and neither page places Sirhind, the Chenab or the Salt Range proper. The disc is the researcher's reading of the page's place names.

ledger.note: 870: with Kabul lost to Ya'qub ibn al-Layth, the Shahis rule from Udabhandapura. Infobox: "Capital: Kabul (822–870); Udabhandapura (870–1001)". The page does not say when Lalliya moved the capital; the dynasty itself is dated "c. 822".

region.text: Kabul and the country down to Lamghan, recaptured by Lalliya

ledger.note: 878: Lalliya retakes Kabul from the Saffarids. "The region was in Saffarid control until 878 CE before being recaptured by Lalliya, the successor to Samanta." Kabul is the page's land; Laghman is the researcher's addition from the Jayapala page's "Lamghan".

region.text: In 986–987, Jayapala marched towards Ghazni and met with Sabuktigin's forces at Ghuzak.

ledger.note: 986: Jayapala marches on Ghazni. "In 986–987, Jayapala marched towards Ghazni and met with Sabuktigin's forces at Ghuzak." The Jayapala page adds a treaty (an indemnity of one million Shahi dirhams and fifty war elephants, and some frontier forts ceded) that Jayapala repudiated.

region.text: 991: the Ghaznavids rout the Shahis at Laghman

ledger.note: 991: the Ghaznavids rout the Shahis at Laghman. the Ghaznavids routed the Shahis, who fled beyond the Indus; the fighting zone is settled in Sabuktigin's favour the same year.

region.text: the whole territory up to Peshawar

ledger.note: 991: Sabuktigin takes everything up to Peshawar. The Jayapala page says the whole territory up to Peshawar was lost and Sabuktigin installed his own tax-collectors; Peshawar returned to the Shahis soon after (undated), so the Pakistani part of Gandhara stays Shahi.

minus.text: Nandana, Jailam (Jhelum) and Takeshar, the Salt Range and Jhelum country that Bharat of Lahore wished to wrest from Jayapala

ledger.note: 998-999: Jayapala annexes Lahore. The Jayapala page says he annexed Lahore around 998–999, after Chandrak was captured near Samutla; the Anandapala page confirms that Lahore had been annexed by the Shahis around 998–999 under Jayapala. The year is the later of the two; the page gives a range. The Nandana-Jhelum disc is held already (Jayapala page: Bharat of Lahore contested Nandana, Jailam and Takeshar c. 990-991), so only the Lahore country outside it is a gain.

region.text: Peshawar and Gandhara annexed by the Ghaznavids

ledger.note: 1001: after the battle at Peshawar the Shahis lose everything west of the Indus. Infobox: "Peshawar and Gandhara annexed by the Ghaznavids"; "Within a few months, the entire Shahi territory to the west of the Indus had submitted to Mahmud" (Jayapala page). Day of the battle: the Battle of Peshawar page gives 27 November 1001 in its infobox and in its body ("The two armies clashed on 27 November 1001 CE"), as does the Hindu Shahis infobox; the Hindu Shahis and Jayapala bodies say 27 September 1001. The dedicated battle page is followed, so month 11 stands (re-read 2026-10-19).
1002: the Shahi seat moves to Nandana after Hund falls. Infobox: "Nandana (1002–1014)"; Anandapala "ascended to the throne around April 1002".

1008: Mahmud invades the Shahi country across the Indus. Infobox: "Battle of Chach: 31 December 1008"; the Anandapala page has Mahmud invade in about December 1008. The body says "C. December 1008". Chach lies on the east bank of the Indus; the zone is the researcher's reading.

1009: Anandapala makes peace with Mahmud. the page has Anandapala send an embassy the year after Chach (c. 1009) and Mahmud accept peace; the terms were tributary status, limited military support, passage for Ghaznavid troops and an annual tribute - the Ghaznavid dossier should carry a vassal_start with counterpart hindu-shahis.

union.text: Nandana, Jailam (Jhelum) and Takeshar, the Salt Range and Jhelum country that Bharat of Lahore wished to wrest from Jayapala

ledger.note: 1014: Nandana is sacked and a Ghaznavid governor installed; the territory "west of Tausi" is lost. The page puts the face-off in the middle of 1014 (the Hindu Shahis infobox says March 1014 for Nandana and the Tausi); it gives no boundary, so the whole Rawalpindi-Taxila-Salt Range country is the researcher's reading. Review fix: the Salt Range and Jhelum country round Nandana is added to the region, since Nandana (the capital 1002-1014) is the place sacked.
1015: the Shahi seat is Lahore. Infobox: "Hastika (1014–1015); Lahore (1015–1026)"; the Trilochanapala page is silent on any move to Lahore.
1026: the last Shahi king Bhimapala falls. Infobox: "Annexed by the Ghaznavids: 1026"; "Bhimapala ... continued to rule until 1026; nothing is known about his rule or territories."

wars.name: Shahi-Ghaznavid war of Laghman

zones.text: Kabul valley and Laghman up to Peshawar

wars.outcome: Jayapala met Sabuktigin at Ghuzak (986-987) and agreed a treaty (an indemnity, fifty elephants, some frontier forts) that he repudiated; the Ghaznavids routed the Shahis at Laghman in 991 and took everything up to Peshawar.
wars.note: The page calls the 991 battle Second Laghman; Peshawar later returned to the Shahis (undated).

wars.name: Battle of Peshawar (1001)
wars.outcome: Mahmud of Ghazni routed Jayapala at Peshawar; Jayapala paid 250,000 dinars and 50 elephants with a son and grandson as hostages; all Shahi land west of the Indus submitted.
wars.note: Date 27 November 1001 on this page (infobox and body, re-read 2026-10-19) and in the Hindu Shahis infobox; 27 September in the body of the Hindu Shahis and Jayapala pages. Mahmud returned to Ghazni in April 1002.

wars.name: Mahmud's Multan campaign
wars.outcome: Anandapala refused Mahmud passage to Multan and posted troops on the Indus; Mahmud went to war, Anandapala fled to Kashmir and Mahmud took Multan; no Shahi land is said to change hands.

wars.name: Battle of Chach
wars.outcome: Trilochanapala could not stop Mahmud crossing the Indus; "The Battle of Chach ended with the defeat of the Hindu Shahis"; Mahmud seized Nagarkot for spoils; peace c. 1009 on tributary terms.
wars.note: Infobox date 31 December 1008. The page does not mention Waihind.

wars.name: Battle of Nandana

union.text: Nandana, Jailam (Jhelum) and Takeshar, the Salt Range and Jhelum country that Bharat of Lahore wished to wrest from Jayapala

wars.outcome: The Nandana fortress was sacked and a Ghaznavid governor installed; the Shahi forces and their Kashmiri battalion (sent by Sangramaraja of the Lohara dynasty under Tunga in 1013) were beaten and the territory "west of Tausi" lost.
wars.note: Hindu Shahis infobox: Nandana and River Tausi, March 1014; the Trilochanapala page: the middle of 1014.

certainty.note: No treaty line survives on any page opened; the Indus is the one stable limit after 1001; the Lahore and Salt Range frontiers are approximate.

notes: Cliopatria has no Hindu Shahi row; its Turk Shahis row ends 874. The dossier starts in 870 to follow the turk-shahis dossier (Kabul kingdom 665-870 with the rename to the Hindu Shahi dynasty in 822); the Hindu Shahis page itself dates the dynasty c. 822-1026. Dates inside the pages disagree: Peshawar 27 November (infobox, battle page) or 27 September (bodies); Anandapala's death c. late 1010 (not 1013). The Anandapala and Trilochanapala pages are silent on Lahore as capital, on Waihind and on Hastika's site. The Hindu Shahis infobox lists the rulers with approximate accession years (c. 822 Kallar, c. 850 Samanta, c. 880 Lalliya, c. 903 Toramana, c. 921 Bhimadeva, 964-1001 Jayapala, c. 1002 Anandapala, c. 1010 Trilocanapala, c. 1021 Bhimapala); identity.rulers carries them from 870 with each end year taken from the next accession, so the strip is a convention, not a documented regnal list (review fix 2026-10-19). Maps: the Ghaznavid dossier should record vassal_start (1009, counterpart hindu-shahis) and the gains in 991, 1001, 1014 and 1026. Gazetteer names wanted: Udabhandapura/Hund (Attock, Pakistan), Nandana (Salt Range), Kangra/Nagarkot, Hastika; Ghaznavid Empire's Cliopatria shape already covers part of Gandhara from 1000, the dossier's keyframes are the reference for 870-1026. Review fixes 2026-10-19: (1) the Salt Range and Jhelum country (70 km disc round Nandana, 32.7 N 72.9 E) is added to keyframes 1-5, to the 1014 loss and to the Battle of Nandana zone, so the capital Nandana lies inside the state; the Jayapala page names Nandana, Jailam and Takeshar as Jayapala's c. 990-991. (2) The rest of the Punjab east of the Indus before 999 (Chenab doab, Sirhind to Multan in the Jayapala page's extent sentence) is NOT drawn: no page places a town there, Lahore came only in 998-999 and Multan was Daud's. (3) Peshawar day: the battle page itself says 27 November in infobox and body; month 11 kept. Disagreement with the reviewer: none. wars/2 and wars/4 belligerents were already corrected by the reviewer (emirate-of-multan, lohara-dynasty).
